title: What Actually Is a CPU?
sources: Wikipedia, 'Apple M4': the M4 chip has 28 billion transistors (modern processors hold billions of transistors)
Baeldung / Codecademy 'The instruction cycle' / Save My Exams 'The fetch-decode-execute cycle': a CPU repeatedly fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it, executes it, then moves to the next
Intel, 'What Is Clock Speed?': clock speed is measured in GHz; a 3.2 GHz processor runs 3.2 billion cycles per second
Intel / Corsair 'CPU clock speed explained': modern CPUs have multiple cores, each able to process instructions on its own
TechSpot, 'The Science of Keeping It Cool': transistors switching on and off draw current and turn electrical energy into heat, which is why processors need cooling

Transistors act as electronic switches whose on/off states represent binary 1 and 0; logic gates built from them perform arithmetic (standard computer architecture, e.g. Cognito KS3 'The CPU & Fetch-Decode-Execute')

lines.text: What actually is a CPU, and why is it called your computer's brain?
lines.caps: WHAT *ACTUALLY | IS A *CPU | AND *WHY | IS IT *CALLED | YOUR COMPUTER'S *BRAIN?

lines.text: packed with billions of tiny switches called transistors.
Each switch is just on or off, a one or a zero,
lines.caps: EACH *SWITCH | IS JUST *ON | OR *OFF | A *ONE | OR A *ZERO

lines.text: but flip them in clever patterns and they can do math.
lines.caps: BUT *FLIP THEM | IN CLEVER *PATTERNS | AND *THEY | CAN DO *MATH

lines.text: Its whole job is one simple loop:
fetch an instruction, decode it, run it, and repeat.
A three gigahertz chip ticks three billion times every second.
Here's the twist: one brain isn't enough anymore,
so modern chips pack several cores, little CPUs working side by side.
lines.caps: SO MODERN *CHIPS | PACK SEVERAL *CORES | LITTLE *CPUS | WORKING *SIDE | BY *SIDE

lines.text: And all that flipping is why your laptop gets warm.
